name: Temporal Color Histogram
description: Tracks color histogram changes over time
algorithm: Temporal Color Histogram — Statistical Pattern Analyzer
mechanism:
This method analyzes temporal color histogram evolution for deepfake detection:

1. **Regional Color Histograms**: Per-frame color histograms are computed for multiple regions: face, skin, hair, background, and clothing. Histograms use perceptually uniform color bins (Lab color space) for meaningful color comparison.

2. **Histogram Temporal Smoothness**: The evolution of color histograms over time should be smooth. The method measures frame-to-frame histogram distance (EMD, chi-squared) and detects anomalous spikes. Deepfake generation may produce frame-to-frame color distribution jumps as the generator's color output varies.

3. **Inter-Region Histogram Correlation**: Color changes in different regions should be correlated (same illumination affects all regions similarly). The method checks temporal correlation between regional histograms. Low face-background histogram correlation indicates the face color evolves independently from scene lighting — a deepfake signature.

4. **Histogram Shape Analysis**: The shape of color histograms encodes content characteristics. The method tracks histogram shape metrics (modes, spread, skewness) over time. Authentic video maintains consistent histogram shapes within the same scene. Deepfake generation may produce fluctuating histogram shapes.

5. **Long-Range Histogram Consistency**: The method compares histograms between frames separated by longer intervals. Scenes with stable lighting should show consistent histograms regardless of temporal distance. Systematic histogram drift without lighting change indicates gradual color shift from AI generation artifacts.
parameters:
Analysis type: statistical
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through temporal color histogram analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video

references.title: Zheng, Y. et al. (2021). Exploring Temporal Coherence for More General Video Face Forgery Detection. ICCV.
